newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wah Tak Fung seen up on debut but concerns linger.
newsitem.headline: Wah Tak Fung seen up on debut but concerns linger.

text.p: Shares of property developer Wah Tak Fung Holdings Ltd are expected to stage a positive debut on Monday, buoyed by good sentiment in the overall stock market, analysts said on Thursday.

But debut gains for the Hong Kong grade B property developer might not be sustained for long due to worries over its high gearing ratio and its exposure to the relatively weak office property sector, they warned.

"Current positive market conditions certainly give the company a boost," said Kinson Au, an analyst at PW Asia. "But all their on-going projects will be completed by 1997 and the perfromance of B grade offices is not encouraging."
Wah Tak Fung's gearing ratio would be reduced from 104 percent to 73 percent following the new issue, but Au said the lower figure was still high.
Its business was not particularly attractive and both office and residential properties showed signs of slowing down in the third quarter, said Aaron Ho, an analyst at Cheerful Securities.
"Certinaly residential developers are more attractive than office developers," he added.
The response of Wah Tak Fung's 138 million share initial public offering was indifferent at around 10 times subscription.
The grey market price of the shares, offered at HK$1.88 per share, was currently about HK$2 per share, analysts said.
"I bet it rises to HK$2.20 at most," Au said.
Wah Tak Fung has a land bank of 44,700 sq metres with existing properties valued at HK$2.565 billion as at June 30, 1996.
